A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DocVAL. All 15 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–E report original benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative examples for document question answering and localization.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, and Appendix G adds experiments testing validator threshold and component-weight sensitivity.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the teacher–student pipeline, five validator modules, training objective, two-stage refinement and OCR-free inference. The new sensitivity experiments vary existing parameters without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use DocVQA, VisualMRC, FUNSD, CORD and SROIE. The new sensitivity studies use DocVQA; additional document regimes and constrained prediction domains are discussed without new evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ARIAL, using Gemma3-27B and TrOCR, with results on four retained benchmarks. Existing comparators remain unchanged. DOGR and TRIG receive conceptual comparisons in Appendix F.1 but are not empirically evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces controlled DocVQA experiments varying the quality threshold from 0.75 to 0.95 and testing six component-weight configurations, including associated retention and dataset-size changes. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, model configurations and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 10–11 newly test whether performance depends strongly on validator thresholds and weights. Appendix H.1 adds a training-stage cost analysis. Existing detector, teacher, validation, iteration and data-scale ablations, alongside qualitative cases, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Appendix G reports variation across parameter configurations, rather than statistical uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the 4B model's CORD ANLS from 85.5 to 85.6. New ARIAL results include DocVQA 88.7 ANLS/50.1 mAP; DocVAL-12B remains at 91.4/82.4. Tables 10–11 add sensitivity results, including mAP ranges of 80.8–82.4 for thresholds 0.80–0.90 and 81.2–82.4 across weights. Appendix H.1 adds relative wall-clock results.

T1.justification: The training loss, quality-score definitions and convergence equations remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. Relocated equations and empirical explanations of sensitivity introduce no new mathematical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The framework, 95K dataset, data-efficiency and deployment contributions remain unchanged. Section 5.1 qualifies the state-of-the-art claim to compact, end-to-end, OCR-free-at-inference VLMs and adds an explicit claim of outperforming modular grounding baselines on overlapping benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for the ARIAL performance gap and validator sensitivity, plus explicit limitations concerning degraded scans and chart-dominant pages. The handwriting failure already appeared in v2. New discussion also extends potential applicability to forecasting and other constrained prediction domains.

D1.justification: Appendix H.1 newly documents approximately 228K versus 251K example-passes for B1 and B2, and B2 wall-clock cost of 1.0–1.2 times B1. These expand documentation of the existing schedule and hardware. The shortened GitHub label retains the same code/data destination.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and Appendix F substantially expand positioning against ARIAL, MGA-VQA, DOGR, TRIG and concurrent distillation approaches. Appendix A and the discussion add connections to biometric recognition, secure communication, optimization, forecasting and model compression. This extends research positioning beyond bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. v3 adds focused comparison and ablation explanations, Appendices F–H, and applicability paragraphs, alongside bibliographic, correspondence-email and publication-footer edits.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an ARIAL row, OCR-at-inference column and caption qualification. Tables 8–11 add comparison and sensitivity displays; Table 8 redisplays Table 1 scores with differences. Figure 2 is enlarged with unchanged artwork, and appendix equations, tables and examples reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix G adds useful evidence about validator sensitivity that v2 lacked, while Appendix H improves transparency about training costs and applicability limits. These gains are bounded by testing sensitivity on only DocVQA without run uncertainty. The new comparison narrative also overstates some evidence: Table 8 claims superiority in both metrics on every overlapping benchmark despite providing no SROIE mAP comparison.
